entries.navigation_reason: People walk a square lattice over the area this ground states or declares: a flat ground has no paths of its own, so the lattice is the route graph this entry chooses, at the spacing below.
entries.arrival_reason: A person arrives where the starter's snapshot states its spawn, and the society reads that point from the world: nobody starts on it or within 2,000 mm of it, and a successor that moves it is refused.
entries.floor_reason: The starter's own ground module states the ground people stand on, and the app draws it; the society reads it and declares nothing more to stand on.
entries.population_reason: A society on this ground starts with eight people. Its area is a square about 23 metres across with 121 places to stand, and a population sized for a district (128) would stand people on top of each other from the first minute; a handful reads as people living somewhere. Eight is also what one comparison of models runs (the comparison protocol's population_maximum), so every society made here can be compared.
entries.lattice_reason: People route over a square lattice at this spacing. A flat ground has no paths of its own, so a route graph over it is a choice this entry makes rather than a fact the world states. Two metres keeps every point of the area within 1,415 mm of a lattice node, which is inside the reviewed object reach, and keeps a 24 m area at 121 nodes and 220 edges. Every stored input records the spacing it was composed with, so another figure is a new navigation profile, never an edit of this one.
entries.declared_area_reason: Where the ground states no edge (the endless plane every new starter uses), the society declares a square of this half extent about the region origin and says in its input that it did; the stored world stays endless. The figure keeps the lattice at 121 nodes, which holds one tick of 128 people near a tenth of a second, and it equals the only bounded starter ground the product has shipped, so an old and a new starter give a society the same area and the same node identities.
entries.reason: The ground of a saved world made from the built-in starter: a flat authored region whose society walks a lattice over the area the ground states or, where it states none, the area declared here. Read by the society's ground builder, which composes over it, and by the repository, which starts a society over it with this population.
entries.place_dependency_reason: People walk a lattice this ground states or declares, which is no place a producer makes from the world's records, so its input names none.
entries.record_subjects_reason: A lattice's people use only the objects a person placed; the world states no records of its own an activity could name.
entries.population_kind_reason: A starter's people are the villagers every saved world begins with: people who walk, rest, visit and talk by the routine, whom a chosen model or the world's owner may decide for.
entries.minute_cost_reason: This ground states a head count, so it states no measured cost of a minute.
entries.minute_share_reason: This ground states a head count, so it states no share of a minute.

The app draws it as a floor in every region, so a person sees what people and placed objects stand on, and furniture and the small square can be placed on it where nothing was reconstructed.
entries.population_reason: Eight people, as on the starter's ground: a made world's region states no extent, so its society declares the same 24 m square and walks the same lattice (navigation profile authored-ground-lattice/v1), and the figure that suits that area suits it here. entries.lattice_reason: The same two metre lattice as the starter's navigation profile, which this ground shares: every point of the area within 1,415 mm of a node, inside the reviewed object reach. entries.declared_area_reason: A made world states no ground, so the society declares a square of this half extent about the region origin, the area the starter's lattice and population were measured over. entries.navigation_reason: People walk the surfaces the world's own city records state: each footway beside its kerb, round each block's corner toward the curb its record names as next, across a carriageway only on a crossing record, and in and out of a premises through its entrance, as the city place producer derives them (exulanica/world/society_city_place.py) from the navigation table the city grammar's descriptor states. The graph is the world's, not a choice this entry makes, so it states no lattice.
entries.arrival_reason: A person arrives where the world's snapshot states its spawn, which the world's composer derived by one rule when it generated the world: the standing spot its walking surfaces offer nearest the centre of the world's extent. The society reads that point from the world, as it reads the starter's.
entries.floor_reason: The world's own records state every surface a person stands on, and the app draws the world's baked tiles; the society declares nothing more to stand on.
entries.population_reason: A society on this ground holds the people the town's homes house: each premises of homes with a door onto the walking surfaces houses the people its use class and the floor area its record states give it, and where the routine's policy states how many people a new town starts with, that many are spread over the homes (exulanica/world/society_city_place.py). This entry states no head count, which the figure 0 says: how many people a host admits is read from minute_cost, the measured cost of a minute, against the share of the host's slowest minute stated here. A town whose homes house nobody starts no society.
entries.lattice_reason: This ground walks the world's own surfaces and states no lattice, so it states no spacing.
entries.declared_area_reason: The world states its own extent, the tiles it covers, and its surfaces run to its edge, so the society declares no area: it walks the rectangle the world's tiles cover, a walking clearance beyond each edge so that a footway at the edge stays inside it.
entries.reason: The ground of a world generated from a recipe of the city grammar: the streets, footways, crossings and premises its own records state. entries.record_subjects_reason: A town's people use its premises and its street furniture, each the subject of a record of the town's own.
entries.population_kind_reason: A town generated from words is peopled by villagers until its own kind of people is stated here.

entries.minute_cost_reason: What one simulated minute of a society over a town was measured to take, for each engine a town's society is made with, in place of a head count. The living town (exulanica-society/v5) and the society of things (exulanica-society/v7) were measured in one run, on the small town preset and on a market town 384 m long with cross streets 140 m apart and three to five storeys; the record is named by its profile and digest, with its machine. The purposeful society (exulanica-society/v2) was measured with scripts/measure_generated_world.py at 128 people only, and no record of that run was kept. A town is read on the smallest measured graph at or above its own walking nodes, between the nearest measured populations (exulanica/world/society_minute_cost.py). A figure read past the last measured point, by people or by walking nodes, is an estimate and is served as one. What would move these figures: a measurement at more people or on larger graphs, a faster planner, or another machine, whose host states its own scale (EXULANICA_MINUTE_COST_SCALE).
entries.minute_share_reason: A chosen budget, not a measurement: a society over this ground may take a tenth of the host's slowest minute at the 95th percentile, the longest wait the host leaves between two simulated minutes (its base interval at its slowest speed; 8 s where a host states none, so 800 ms). The minute is planned in the application's own process, and a tenth leaves nine tenths of the interval to everything else that process does. A society admitted at the slowest speed may be played at a faster one, where its minute takes a larger share of the wait. A host that wants more people gives its minutes a longer interval or runs a faster machine and states its scale.

entries.navigation_reason: People walk the surfaces the world's own site records state: the corridors each zone keeps clear along its front, its sides and the lane before its areas, a lattice over the rest of its walkable ground, the paths, and the ways to each structure's door, each area's access point and each fixture people use, as the site place producer derives them (exulanica/world/society_site_place.py). The graph is the world's, not a choice this entry makes, so it states no lattice.
entries.arrival_reason: A person arrives where the world's snapshot states its spawn, on the spine a few metres in from the entry, which the site composer derived when it generated the world; the society reads that point from the world, as it reads a town's.
entries.floor_reason: The world's own records state every surface a person stands on, all on the level ground a site stands on, and the app draws them; the society declares nothing more to stand on.
entries.population_reason: A society on this ground holds one inhabitant for each place in a home the world's destinations offer: the sleepers of the beds in its homes' rooms, a home's use class where it has no beds, and the people its kind brings in from homes off the site. The figure is the most people the rule may produce; a world whose homes hold more is refused by name, and every world a kind makes was held to this ceiling by the kind's own checks before the kind was admitted. Measured with scripts/measure_living_site.py on 2026-10-06, a site near the walking graph's bound (879 places, 36 destinations) at 128 people and a market town (918 places) at 128 in the same run: one living tick took 14 ms at the median and 32 ms at the 95th percentile on the site and 12 and 30 ms on the town, over 240 minutes each on a loaded development machine (31 to 39 percent idle), so the site is held to the town's figure.
entries.lattice_reason: This ground walks the world's own surfaces and states no lattice, so it states no spacing.
entries.declared_area_reason: The world states its own extent, the site's width and depth, and its surfaces run to its edge, so the society declares no area: it walks the rectangle the site covers, a walking clearance beyond each edge.
entries.reason: The ground of a world generated from a world kind by the site grammar: the paths, yards, doors, fields and fixtures its own records state. Read by the society's ground builder, which dispatches on the entry's navigation and floor forms, and by the repository, which starts a society over it with the population its rule derives from the world's destinations.

entries.record_subjects_reason: A site's people use its structures, areas and fixtures, and the home at its entry of everybody who lives off the site, each the subject of a record of the site's own.
entries.population_kind_reason: A site generated from a world kind is peopled by villagers until its own kind of people is stated here.
entries.minute_cost_reason: A site's society is held to the head count this entry states, which was measured at 128 people only, so this entry states no measured points. The measurement that would replace the head count is the town's, run over a site at several populations.
